items.title: Opaque menus and selects on a phone
items.dedupe_of: O-404 (the owner's order of 2026-11-19 that dropdowns and popups be glassy), its phone half
items.evidence: Master: below 30rem (sheet-width.ts:13) a Select stamps data-surface="opaque" (SelectContent.vue:132), and so does a DropdownMenu opened from a dock (DropdownMenuContent.vue:84-85, :105). A menu outside a dock was never opaque (:79-83). release/11.1.1, commit ca17dd857 "a phone popup is glass": SelectContent.vue:162 and DropdownMenuContent.vue:87-89 and :120 stamp data-plate="firm". The firm plate is the overlay veil and blur at glass level 0.35, falling to the solid card only under reduced transparency or forced colours (surface-axis.css:99-113 there). Witness: tests-visual/release-11-1-1.spec.ts:204 and :241 ('glass' cells), RED on v11.1.0 and GREEN on the branch, Chromium and WebKit 2287 at 390 touch, rows 4.86 to 10.10:1. The CHANGELOG's top section names the attribute change. O-413's G10 (atlas: hover cards, menus and selects opaque paper with no blur at 1440) reads another glass line: its cause d3d525806 (--glass-chrome-paper: 100%) sits on u/b7-glass and u/dp-integ-glass and is not an ancestor of master, whose glass.css:72 and :91 keep the 20 px floating blur.
items.row: All six surfaces are Selects at sheet width or dock menus below 30rem, the two forms ca17dd857 moves to the firm glass plate, so no new row. This is also the phone half of the owner's O-404; at 1440 these surfaces are glass on master (color's audit reads alpha 0.22 to 0.26). The CHANGELOG already tells a stylesheet that targeted data-surface="opaque" on these two surfaces to target data-plate="firm". The surfaces that stay opaque do so by the sites' own props: daraksha's picker sheet and Gallery (D-03), fourier's four dialogs (F-19). color's space sheet width is C-06. atlas's opaque desktop paper (O-413 G10) is a different tree and is placed with O-413, not here. The check after publish is the 390 frames of the same six surfaces.
items.reply: This is fixed in 11.1.1. Below 30rem a Select and a dock's menu are now glass, firmed so every row reads at 4.5:1, and solid only under reduced transparency. The surfaces your sites made opaque with their own prop are yours to change.

items.title: One opening for menus, selects, popovers, hover cards and tooltips
items.dedupe_of: O-410 (the owner's dropdown-opening order); O-313(d) and O-349(6) for the popover's clock
items.evidence: release/11.1.1 removes the blur, scale and squish from the popover and hover-card entrance (13573d28b): both enter on opacity and a 0.5rem slide (reveal.css:63-71, :103-111 there; PopoverContent.vue:173 binds the panel role, content.ts maps it to the overlay register). Tooltips fade in on 200 ms (reveal.css:128-145; motion-registers.css:83-88; --duration-fast 0.2s, scheme-motion.css:101). Every popup turns back from where it stands (001a726e8). The menu and Select grow from the trigger as a clip transition on --spring-bloom (reveal.css:270-307 there), no fade-in, no blur; its clock is still 0.37 s (scheme-spring.css:106) and the curve reaches 0.9 near 62 %, about 230 ms (scheme-spring.css:63). On master it is still the glass-menu-grow keyframe (reveal.css:277-290). The popover still enters on --enter-overlay-clock = --spring-panel-duration, 0.45 s on a curve that peaks at 1.042 (motion-registers.css:69-70; scheme-spring.css:105). The 11.1.2 scope disagrees with itself on that clock: glass-11.1.1-scope.md:81 carries O-313(d) ('the popover on the menu register', animation/INBOUND-ROWS.md:9), while :95 carries O-349's 'The Popover enters on the panel clock with no blur ramp', which 11.1.1 has already built.
items.row: 11.1.1 cures three of the five complaints: blur in motion, the tooltip's missing entrance, and reversal mid-way. What remains is one change, the opening's form and clock for all five surfaces, and the popover's 450 ms clock is part of it. Moving the popover from 450 ms to about 200 ms changes every consumer's popover entrance. That is a changed default, so it is not a patch whatever O-313(d)'s booking said, and the scope's own later line (:95) keeps the panel clock. Correction to the earlier placement: O-313(d)'s clock half leaves 11.1.2 and folds into O-410. The orchestrator strikes it from line 81's carry, or restates line 95. One opening (out of the trigger, by shape, read as done by 200 ms) is the owner's O-410. It changes every popup's default entrance and is neither dock nor Metric work, so it goes to 11.3.0, decided on P3's films: each variant opened, and opened then closed within 60 ms, on a menu and a select at 390 and 1440.
items.reply: 11.1.1 already removes the blur, gives tooltips an entrance and lets every popup turn back mid-way. One opening for menus, selects, popovers, hover cards and tooltips, out of the trigger and done by about 200 ms, comes in 11.3.0 once the dropdown prototype is filmed. The popover's quicker clock comes with it.

items.title: The phone form of a short select
items.dedupe_of: O-292a row 17 (a 390 Select bounded with its trigger in view, 11.1.2), for the half that is a defect
items.evidence: Master: below 30rem every Select opens as a sheet anchored to a virtual edge at the viewport's foot (SelectContent.vue:55-65, :77-85; sheet-width.ts:13), whatever the list's length or where its trigger sits. The form was atlas's ask (U/B7 D-6, cited at SelectContent.vue:55). The exit jump is cured on release/11.1.1 by b0748ff69 ("a popup closes in the form it opened in"): the sheet keeps its form and slides out (reveal.css:257-259, :315-317 there). Already booked: fourier's critique (audit/inbound-critiques/fourier-for-glass-2026-11-12.md, /morph 390 SelectContent, 'the list covers the whole viewport, the dock and its trigger included; correct: bounded to the trigger's region with the trigger in view') is O-292a row 17 (INBOUND.md:316), carried for 11.1.2 at glass-11.1.1-scope.md:87 ('SelectContent bounded at 390 with its trigger in view').
items.row: Three parts. (1) The exit jump is 11.1.1's and is built. (2) A phone list that never covers its own trigger is already a booked 11.1.2 defect (O-292a row 17); it bounds the sheet and keeps today's form, so it is a patch. The earlier placement missed it. (3) The form rule itself (anchored for a short list, a sheet for a long one) changes the narrow-width default of every consumer's Select. atlas asked for the sheet and value.js asks for the anchored list, so the owner picks, for 11.3.0. Default offered: a list of seven rows or fewer with no search field opens anchored at its trigger on 11.1.1's firm plate; a longer list, or one with a search, keeps the sheet. O-399 and LF-40 (a Select inside a Sheet, 11.1.2) rule that case's form first and should take the same rule so the two do not diverge. Seating the sheet above a foot dock (O-348, O-352) stays in 11.1.2.
items.reply: 11.1.1 makes the phone list leave the way it came, and 11.1.2 keeps a phone list from covering its own trigger. Opening a short list at its trigger instead of as a sheet would change every site's phone selects, so it goes to the owner for 11.3.0 with this default: seven rows or fewer, with no search, open at the trigger.

items.title: Type on a phone
items.evidence: --type-caption is clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem) (scale.css:99-103), 12.2 px at 390. It is read by SegmentedTabs labels (segmented.css:195), Badge sm (badge/index.ts:69), Metric's context, unit and delta (metric/styles.css:55, :81, :99), Label's requirement mark (Label.vue:114), tooltip text (offsets.css:102) and the dock layer group (layer-group.css:256). On a coarse pointer --control-text-sm floors at 16 × 6/7 = 13.71 px (light-dark.css:35); Button xs and sm read it (button/styles.css:234, :240), as does ToggleGroup (toggle-group/styles.css:86). --type-micro is a fixed 11 px (scale.css:86), read by EasingCurve's "0" and "1" (EasingCurve.vue:186-187, no prop to hide them; props at :42-60) and the kbd cap (base-misc.css:234). --configurator-section-size is --type-heading, 25.9 px at every width (sizing-config.css:40).
items.row: Every part is a changed default of the type scale or a new prop, so this is a minor, in line with the owner's verbatim 'most apps have text that's too small' (ORDER.md, FORTY-SECOND). The Metric's caption-step text goes with the Metric voice pass (O-344, 11.2.0). SegmentedTabs on --control-text is already W-E.7's line in PLAN.md:156 (unplaced) and comes into 11.3.0 with the rest: the caption floor at 13 px (clamp minimum 0.8125rem); --control-text-sm's coarse floor at 14 px; --type-micro raised to the caption floor rather than removed (removal would be 12.0.0); an EasingCurve prop that hides the endpoint labels; and a narrow-width value for --configurator-section-size (default --type-subheading, 20.4 px). The exact floors are the study's own numbers (STUDY.md section 9), so the build shows the owner one before-and-after frame per app.
items.reply: Glass raises its floors in 11.3.0: captions to 13 px, control and tab labels to 14 px, nothing left at 11 px, an option to hide the easing glyph's 0 and 1, and a smaller phone size for the configurator's section title. The Metric's small text moves with the Metric voice change in 11.2.0.

items.title: Whether 1.25 becomes the coarse control scale's default
items.evidence: --ui-coarse-scale: 1.5 (sizing.css:20) becomes --ui-scale under (pointer: coarse), and --control-floor rises to the 44 px target (light-dark.css:17-20). Heights are 28/36/40/44 px × scale, floored (sizing.css:26-29), and the glyph is 1rem × scale (sizing.css:53). Type does not scale on touch (light-dark.css:34-36). The dock does not read the scale on touch: --dock-scale is var(--dock-mobile-scale, 1) (dock/styles/density.css:380). At 1.25 the rungs are 44 (xs, by the floor), 45, 50 and 55 px, and the glyph is 20 px. Glass's answer of 19 Nov (ORDER.md, 'Glass answers to the study'): the sites may set 1.25 now; whether it becomes the default is open, a minor, weighed with G4. 11.2.0's ready list is closed ('this list and nothing more', RULINGS-7.md, 'The final ready list'; 'Not in 11.2.0: ... a preset beyond ControlsDock').
items.row: The sites' 1.25 line is public theming and has already been answered. Making 1.25 the default changes the touch size of every consumer's controls (not the dock, not type), so it is a minor and the owner's look. It is the controls' half of the owner's padding order (O-409); that order's dock half is the redesign's seat and glyph rulings. As glass answered, it is judged together with G4 (dock density on touch). It cannot join 11.2.0, whose ready list is closed, and it is not 12.0.0's base-size collapse. Default offered: yes, 1.25 in 11.3.0, judged on the four sites' before-and-after frames with their own 1.25 line in place. The sites drop that line at the release, and the 44 px floor keeps every target whole.
items.reply: Your 1.25 line is fine as theming now. Making 1.25 glass's own default is the owner's call. We will offer it for 11.3.0, weighed with dock density and using your frames as the evidence, and after that the sites can drop their line.

items.title: The sheet: chrome floor, snap-back, handle-only drag
items.evidence: The floor (sheet/styles.css:538-553 on master; :554-564 on release/11.1.1) sums the plate's padding and seam, the grip's 44 px, two gutters, the crown's seam, one line, and a footer seam plus a 44 px action. It counts the crown and footer whether or not the sheet draws them (no condition on the selector), about 204 px in all, and binds top and bottom sheets only. Snap-back: cured on release/11.1.1 by 0fec2b3f3, which seats the spring at the drag's value and speed on release (detents/use.ts:305-308 there). The path is the same for every side (axisCoord, use.ts:85-96 there), but its witness (992ceb2a0) ran a bottom sheet at 390 touch; keyframes' 844x390 case is a side sheet (inv-phone.md section 6). Drag: the grip and the header always drag, and the body drags from its leading edge (detents/use.ts:62, :89-101 on master), with no prop to change that. Inner scroll: the detented body already has overflow-y: auto and overscroll-behavior: contain (sheet/styles.css:191-199).
items.row: Four parts. (1) The snap-back is cured in 11.1.1 (0fec2b3f3). keyframes' 844x390 film, re-shot after publish, is the side-sheet check the 11.1.1 witness lacks. (2) Inner scroll is contained on master; the case where scroll chains to the page is O-347 (11.1.2). (3) Handle-only drag is LF-16's drag-region prop (grip, chrome or all, with all the default), 11.3.0 per PLACED.md. (4) A rest of the grip plus one row needs a floor that counts only the chrome the sheet draws. That changes the rest heights consumers see today, so it is a minor and joins LF-16 in 11.3.0 as the floor part of W-E.3, which is otherwise unplaced.
items.reply: The landscape snap-back is fixed in 11.1.1, and the sheet's body already keeps its own scroll. A grip-only drag option and a floor low enough for a one-row peek come in 11.3.0.

items.title: Focus rings: default squares, a kept ring, a ringed row
items.dedupe_of: O-337 (the focus-ring floor; LF-39 is its duplicate), with O-397 (the ring follows a rounded control)
items.evidence: FadingScroll's port is tabindex="0" (FadingScroll.vue:67), and no :focus-visible rule in src reaches .fading-scroll or .segmented-tab (the selectors at a11y-overrides.css:114-135 and base.css:144 name neither), so the browser draws its default ring (fourier audit row 15: 'outline: auto 1px', square). The .segmented-tab button (SegmentedTabs.vue:243-253) carries no focus-ring class and segmented.css has no focus rule, though its corner is a stadium (segmented.css:193). The house recipe is .focus-ring:focus-visible (base.css:144-152). DockTrigger's select arm renders reka's own SelectTrigger (DockTrigger.vue:4, :92-107). Only glass's SelectTrigger marks a pointer open (SelectTrigger.vue:52-53), and the mark defaults to "keyboard" (openInput.ts:21), so the rule that drops a pointer-opened list's row ring ([data-open-input="pointer"] .glass-menu-row:focus-visible, menu.css:61-63) never applies to a dock list: K14's frame e-scene-select-1440-rest2s.png shows the ringed row. Select and menu leave the focus return to reka; only Dialog and Sheet use returnFocusQuietly (focus-return.ts:9-14; DialogContent.vue:143, SheetContent.vue:275), and fourier's audit row 30 reads the sections seat matching :focus-visible 0.3 to 2.5 s after a click. Unchanged on release/11.1.1: no commit since v11.1.0 touches these focus paths.
items.row: Three defect cures, joined to the 11.1.2 ring row (O-337's 3:1 floor, LF-39 its duplicate, O-397's ring that follows a rounded control). (1) FadingScroll and SegmentedTabs take the house outline. The tab's ring follows its stadium, and the port's ring is drawn inside the port so its mask (base-misc.css:52-61) does not cut it. (2) DockTrigger's select arm marks the open input on pointerdown and keydown, as glass's SelectTrigger does, so a list opened by a pointer shows the highlight alone. (3) After a pointer pick, a Select's or menu's focus return leaves the trigger without its ring, decided by the same open input. None adds a prop. Witness: RED on v11.1.0 and on release/11.1.1, both engines, at 390 and 1440.
items.reply: In 11.1.2 the scroller and the segmented tabs get glass's own ring at 3:1, following their shape. A dock list opened by a pointer stops ringing its row, and a dock trigger no longer keeps a ring after a mouse pick.

items.title: Select: the chevron and the stepped shadow
items.dedupe_of: O-292a (the chevron); W-B.4's overlay-stack row, folded to W-E.4 (the shadow)
items.evidence: The chevron's in-data-[state=open]:rotate-180 (SelectTrigger.vue:76 on master and on release/11.1.1) matches any open ancestor. It is booked as O-292a row 16 (INBOUND.md:316; glass-11.1.1-scope.md:87, which cites the old line 72). The shadow: [data-slot="select-content"] (overlay-plate.css:302) stacks rim, vivid under-shadow, floating shadow and --shadow-cartoon-lg (overlay-plate.css:340-343), whose three offsets have no blur (shadow.css:86-89). The register declares no box-shadow of its own (overlay-plate.css:44-56), so the menu plate wears its rung's shadow without the stamp. W-B.4 ruled this four-shadow stack a defect ('one cast per floating plate', folded to W-E.4; waves/W-B.4.md:18), and W-E.4 is unplaced (waves/INDEX.md:60). Unchanged on release/11.1.1.
items.row: The chevron is O-292a, in 11.1.2 as booked. The stamp is a defect already ruled, with no release yet: the Select is the one floating plate that carries it. Its cure removes no token (cards keep --shadow-cartoon-lg) and changes no default a consumer chose, so it rides 11.1.2 with the chevron: the Select's plate drops the stamp and matches the menu's. Witness: an open Select's computed box-shadow equals an open menu's, both engines, 1440.
items.reply: Both are glass's and both go in 11.1.2. The chevron turns only for its own Select, and the Select's list loses the stepped shadow so it matches the menus.

items.title: Dialogs: reduced motion, the hidden Close, the veil, the palette's list
items.evidence: Reduced motion: release/11.1.1 9f9719c76 makes a Dialog and a Sheet fade in and out (witness 'fade' cells in release-11-1-1-reduce.spec.ts). CommandDialog's list: release/11.1.1 22e65f1ba keeps CommandList mounted through the dialog's exit (CommandList.vue; witness release-11-1-1.spec.ts:587 'routes' cells, Chromium and WebKit 2287). Close: [data-slot="dialog-close"] is position: absolute with no z-index (dialog/styles.css:100-113) and is authored first in the plate (DialogContent.vue:215-235), so any later positioned or stacking child paints over it. Under scroll the plate is itself the scroller (DialogContent.vue:184), so the close scrolls away with the rows. Its gutter is reserved only on a DialogHeader (styles.css:56-62). daraksha's audit measures the close in the tree, on the corner of the first row's last plate, unseen at both widths (audit/daraksha.md, D-04). Veil: the scrim dims with no backdrop (ModalOverlay.vue:7-14, :80), a centred dialog adds the focus veil's frost core (ModalOverlay.vue:19-28, :87), and the plate is see-through by design (DialogContent.vue:165-170). In e-shortcuts-1440.png the die shows as a blurred red and magenta wash under the right column; the words over it stay legible.
items.row: Two of the four parts are cured in 11.1.1: reduced motion (9f9719c76) and the palette's list (22e65f1ba). The Close is a glass defect for 11.1.2, alongside O-341's close rework: the close paints above the body, stays in view while a scrolling dialog's body scrolls (placed outside the scroller, or sticky), and the body reserves its corner when there is no header. Witness: a headerless scroll Dialog with a full-bleed grid, scrolled, whose close hit-tests to itself at 390 and 1440. The veil over a saturated subject is a look, not a legibility fault (LF-17 covers the light-theme ink). Owner question, 11.3.0. Correction to the earlier default: offer no change. The words read in the frame, and the owner's order of the same day (O-404) asks popups to be more glassy, not less. The 0.35 firm plate goes beside today's plate as the alternative frame.
items.reply: Reduced motion and the palette's closing list are fixed in 11.1.1. In 11.1.2 a scrolling dialog's close button stays on top and in view. Whether a dialog should hide a bright subject more is the owner's choice for 11.3.0; we will offer today's plate with a firmer one beside it.

items.title: LabeledSwitch forces layout for its name
items.evidence: LabeledSwitch gives the Switch an id and aria-labelledby but no aria-label (LabeledSwitch.vue:45-55). reka-ui 2.10.1's SwitchRoot computes aria-label as document.querySelector('[for=id]')?.innerText whenever it has an id (node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Switch/SwitchRoot.js:83). The render reads it unless $attrs["aria-label"] is set ('_ctx.$attrs["aria-label"] || ariaLabel.value', :96), and innerText forces layout. Booked as O-293(c) (INBOUND.md:268; glass-11.1.1-scope.md:72, with a trace witness of no forced layout in the mount task). Not built on release/11.1.1: LabeledSwitch.vue has no commit since v11.1.0.
items.row: A duplicate of O-293(c), in 11.1.2 as booked. keyframes' 63 to 129 ms per phone scene change (inv-speed.md section 7) is a second witness. The cure passes a plain-string label as aria-label, so reka's || never evaluates the innerText read; aria-labelledby still decides the name. A bare Switch with an id and an outside <label for> takes the same path; giving it an aria-label is ordinary naming, not a shim.
items.reply: This is already booked for 11.1.2. LabeledSwitch will hand the switch its label directly, so no layout is forced on each scene change. A plain Switch with an outside label can pass its own aria-label today.

items.title: Menu layouts: a toggle row, one icon column, a submenu in place
items.dedupe_of: O-393 (the tick in a trailing column)
items.evidence: Checkbox and radio items put their check in an absolutely placed leading slot (.menu__indicator, overlay-plate.css:247-255; DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.vue:50). Moving it to a trailing slot is booked as O-393 (glass-11.1.1-scope.md:136-138) and is unchanged on release/11.1.1. A submenu always floats beside its row, with collision avoidance at every width (DropdownMenuSubContent.vue:59-61), and has no phone form. No menu part holds a row of toggle seats above the list.
items.row: (b) is O-393, in 11.1.2 as booked. (a) A head row of three or four toggle seats is a new part for 11.3.0, designed with O-413's G14 (a leading mark in menu and select rows, placement owed) so the two share one row grammar. (c) A submenu that replaces its parent in place below 30rem, with a back row at its head, changes every consumer's narrow submenus. It is a changed default, so 11.3.0.
items.reply: The tick moves to its own trailing column in 11.1.2, so icons share one column. A row of toggles at the head of a menu, and a submenu that replaces its parent on a phone, come in 11.3.0.
